text: For any triangle, when one of the sides is produced, the external angle is greater than each of the internal and opposite angles.  Let $ABC$ be a triangle, and let one of its sides $BC$ have been produced   to $D$. I say that the external angle $ACD$ is greater than each of the  internal and opposite angles, $CBA$ and $BAC$.
Let the (straight-line) $AC$ have been cut in half at (point) $E$ [Prop.~1.10].
And $BE$ being joined, let it have been produced in a straight-line to  (point) $F$.
And let $EF$ be made equal to $BE$ [Prop.~1.3],
and let $AC$ have been drawn through to (point) $G$.
Therefore, since $AE$ is equal to $EC$, and $BE$ to $EF$, the two (straight-lines)  $AE$, $EB$ are equal to the two (straight-lines) $CE$, $EF$, respectively.
assertion: AE, EB equal to CE, EF respectively

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the two (straight-lines)  $AE$, $EB$ are equal to the two (straight-lines) $CE$, $EF$, respectively

text: Also, angle $AEB$ is equal to angle $FEC$, for (they are)  vertically opposite [Prop.~1.15].
assertion: angle AEB equals angle FEC (vertically opposite)

text: Thus, the base $AB$ is equal to the base  $FC$,

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the base $AB$ is equal to the base  $FC$

text: and the triangle $ABE$ is equal to the triangle $FEC$,

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the triangle $ABE$ is equal to the triangle $FEC$

text: and the remaining  angles subtended by the equal sides are equal to the corresponding remaining angles [Prop.~1.4].
assertion: remaining angles subtended by equal sides are equal to corresponding remaining angles

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the remaining  angles subtended by the equal sides are equal to the corresponding remaining angles

assertion: angle ECD is greater than angle ECF
angle ACD is greater than angle BAE

text: Similarly, by having cut $BC$ in half,  it can  be shown (that) $BCG$---that is to say, $ACD$---(is) also greater than $ABC$.
assertion: ACD is also greater than angle ABC
